newsitem.title: USA: Mattel Q1 Barbie, Disney, Tyco sales up.
newsitem.headline: Mattel Q1 Barbie, Disney, Tyco sales up.

text.p: Mattel Inc said Thursday first quarter 1997 sales for Barbie were up 10 percent, Disney sales were up more than 20 percent and Hot Wheels sales nearly doubled, but that Fisher-Price sales were down 29 percent from last year.
The company said in a release that Tyco products were also in strong demand, with a sales increase of 27 percent led by the core brands of Sesame Street, Matchbox and Magna Doodle.

Jill Barad, Mattel's president and chief executive officer, said in the release that worldwide demand for the company's core brands is "extremely strong," and that although Fisher-Price sales were down, a strategy to focus on its core preschool toy business "is working."
The CEO said retail take-away for Fisher-Price toys was up by nine percent and that both Mattel U.S. and worldwide core brand sales, excluding Fisher-Price, were up 19 percent.
Mattel reported net income of $13 million, or $0.05 per share, for the 1997 first quarter before its merger with Tyco Toys Inc and the impact of a charge related to integration and restructuring.
The $0.05 per share is after a negative impact related to the strength of the U.S. dollar, and compares with $0.11 per share in the 1996 quarter, the company said.
Mattel had earlier indicated it expected first quarter earnings to be in the range of $0.01 to $0.04 per share.
The First Call consensus estimate was $0.02 per share for the first quarter of 1997.
First quarter net sales for Mattel alone were $569 million in U.S. dollars, down 3 percent from $586 million in the year-ago quarter, but were flat in local currencies.
